title: Subarray Sum Equals K
corePattern: Prefix Sum with Hash Map Frequency Counting
interviewTips: Clarify: can nums contain negatives and zeros? If only positives, sliding window works, but with negatives you must use prefix sums — ask this explicitly.
Trade-off: Brute force is O(1) space but O(n^2) time; prefix-sum + hash map trades O(n) space for O(n) time by turning subarray sum query sum(j+1..i)=k into prefix[i]-prefix[j]=k lookup.
Edge-case tip: mention prefix sum 0 with frequency 1 upfront to count subarrays starting at index 0, and test k=0 with zeros e.g. [0,0,0] and negative numbers e.g. [1,-1,0].

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Enumeration
approaches.intuition: Every subarray is defined by a start i and end j. Fix i and expand j while maintaining running sum; whenever running sum equals k we found a valid subarray. This directly checks the definition without any preprocessing.
approaches.theory: For each start index i, iterate end index j >= i and maintain cur = sum(nums[i..j]) incrementally as cur += nums[j]. If cur == k increment answer. This enumerates all n*(n+1)/2 subarrays. Correct because all pairs (i,j) are visited and sum is computed exactly. No extra data structure needed, but repeated work causes quadratic time.

timeComplexity.explanation: n start positions, each expands up to n ends. Each inner step is O(1) update and compare, so total ~n^2/2 operations.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only running sum and counters besides input, no extra proportional storage.

edgeCases: Single element equal to k: [5], k=5 -> 1; not equal: [5], k=3 -> 0
Negative numbers: [1,-1,0], k=0 -> 3 ([1,-1], [1,-1,0], [0]) must be counted
All zeros with k=0: [0,0,0] -> 6, tests counting of all subarrays

approaches.name: Approach 2: Prefix Sum + Hash Map
approaches.intuition: Sum of subarray (j+1..i) = prefix[i] - prefix[j]. So we need prefix[j] = prefix[i] - k. While scanning left to right, keep how many times each prefix sum has occurred; for current prefix, the number of valid j is exactly freq[prefix - k].
approaches.theory: Define prefix[0]=0, prefix[i+1]=sum(nums[0..i]). Subarray (l..r) sums to k iff prefix[r+1]-prefix[l]=k iff prefix[l]=prefix[r+1]-k. Iterate r in order, maintain hash map freq of all prefix[l] for l <= r+1 seen so far. Query freq[prefix-k] in O(1) and then insert current prefix. Initialize freq[0]=1 to allow l=0. This counts each valid start exactly once. Works with negatives because it does not assume monotonicity, unlike two-pointers/sliding window.

code.python:
from typing import List
from collections import defaultdict
class Solution:
    def subarraySum(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        freq = defaultdict(int)
        freq[0] = 1
        prefix = 0
        count = 0
        for x in nums:
            prefix += x
            count += freq[prefix - k]
            freq[prefix] += 1
        return count

timeComplexity.explanation: Single pass over n elements, each hash map lookup and update is O(1) average.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Hash map stores up to n+1 distinct prefix sums in worst case.

steps: x=1: prefix=1, need 1-2=-1 -> freq[-1]=0, count=0, freq={0:1,1:1}
x=1: prefix=2, need 2-2=0 -> freq[0]=1, count=1, freq={0:1,1:1,2:1}

edgeCases: Subarray from index 0: [1,2,3], k=3 -> needs freq[0]=1 to count [1,2]
No match and large values: [1000000000,1], k=2 -> 0; watch int range but constraints fit 32-bit prefix (n*1e3 up to 2e7)
